verses.text: Just past the summit, David met Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant. He had two saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a container of wine.

The king asked Ziba, “What's all this for?” Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your household to ride. The bread and fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for anyone who grows faint in the wilderness.”
“Where is your master's grandson?” the king asked. Ziba answered, “He's staying in Jerusalem. He said, ‘Today the people of Israel will give me back my family's kingdom.’”
The king told Ziba, “Everything that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours now.” Ziba said, “I bow before you. May I find favor with you, my lord the king.”
When King David reached Bahurim, a man from Saul's family came out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he came out cursing.
He threw stones at David and all his servants, even though the people and the king's best fighters were on either side of him.
Shimei shouted curses at him: “Get out! Get out, you bloodthirsty man, you villain!

The LORD is making you pay for all the blood shed in Saul's family, whose throne you took. The LORD has given the kingdom to your son Absalom. Your own evil has caught up with you because you've shed so much blood!”
Abishai son of Zeruiah asked the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over there and cut off his head.”
The king answered, “What business is this of yours, you sons of Zeruiah? If he's cursing because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask him why he's doing it?”
David told Abishai and all his servants, “My own son wants me dead. Why be surprised that this man from Benjamin does too? Leave him alone and let him curse. The LORD has told him to.
Maybe the LORD will see the wrong done to me and repay me with good for the curses I've heard today.”
David and his men kept going down the road. Shimei went along the opposite hillside, cursing David, throwing stones at him, and flinging dust.
The king and all the people with him arrived exhausted, and David rested there.
Meanwhile, Absalom and his followers from Israel entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
When David's friend Hushai the Archite came to Absalom, he said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend? Why didn't you go with him?”
Hushai answered, “I will belong to the one the LORD and these people and all Israel have chosen. I'll stay with him.
Besides, who should I serve? Shouldn't I serve his son? Just as I served your father, I'll serve you.”
Then Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Tell us what you think we should do.”

Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father's concubines, the women he left to look after the palace. Then all Israel will hear that your father despises you, and everyone on your side will take courage.”
They put up a tent for Absalom on the palace roof, and he slept with his father's concubines in full view of Israel.
In those days people took Ahithophel's advice as seriously as if they'd asked God himself at the inner sanctuary. That's how both David and Absalom regarded everything Ahithophel advised.
